instruction: I need the background image from the second slide exported as a JPEG file for better compression. Please extract it and save it to the Desktop as "background.jpg". Thanks!

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the background image from slide 1 and exporting it as JPEG format to Desktop. Evaluator checks if the saved file is in JPEG format. Similar complexity to original (extract, process, save).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: extract background from slide 2 (index 1), save as JPEG format, save to Desktop/background.jpg

Getter logic (image.py:56-184): Properly extracts slide background using python-pptx, handles both background fill (type 6) and fallback to largest image on slide, converts expected image to JPEG for fair comparison, returns comprehensive data including hashes, dimensions, formats, and raw image data

Metric logic (image.py:42-156): Implements robust verification with three components: (1) Format check - verifies JPEG format (0.2 points), (2) Dimension check - verifies similar dimensions allowing for conversion variance (0.1 points), (3) Content verification - uses pixel-level MSE comparison to verify actual image content matches (up to 0.7 points based on similarity)

Content verification correctly implemented: Loads both images, resizes for fair comparison, converts to numpy arrays, calculates MSE with appropriate thresholds (MSE<100=0.7pts, MSE<500=0.5pts, MSE<1000=0.3pts, MSE>=1000=0.0pts)
Edge cases handled: Missing files (returns 0.0), dimension mismatches (partial credit), format conversion accounted for (expected image pre-converted to JPEG), comparison errors caught and logged
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: MSE thresholds (100/500/1000) are reasonable but could be empirically validated with sample slide backgrounds to ensure they work across different image types (photos vs graphics)
Minor: Consider adding SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) as an alternative/additional metric for perceptual similarity, though current MSE approach should work well for this use case
